keyCharacteristics: Vermilion means good, favourable, selected or "do this"; solid ink means bad or "avoid". This follows the two-colour logic of the printed almanac.
Square seals with 3px corners and a thin inner white keyline, set in Noto Serif TC Black.
Classical text (卦辭, 爻辭, 籤詩) is set in 楷書 (LXGW WenKai TC). Modern prose uses the system sans; headings use Song serif.
One authored motion, 落印: a seal stamps in.
Phone first. The bottom tabs are 今日, 卜卦, 求籤, 塔羅 and 全部; at 1100px and wider the grouped navigation moves into the top bar.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Good is vermilion and bad is ink, everywhere. Green never means "good", and red never means "bad".

rules.name: The Pigment Rule
rules.body: A section pigment appears only inside a seal. It never tints the page, a card or the text.

rules.name: The Classical Hand Rule
rules.body: Any quotation of a source text is set in 楷書. Plain-language explanation is never set in 楷書.

rules.name: The 落印 Rule
rules.body: The only authored entrance is stamp. It runs for 0.5s with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); it scales from 1.32 to 1, rotates from −7° to 0 and clears a 3px blur. It applies to page seals, the current tab, 宜 and 忌, verdict tones and score seals. With reduced motion, the seal is already stamped.

dos: Do stamp every verdict as a seal; let plain prose carry the explanation.
Do keep the ground cool stone-grey; if it drifts toward cream, it is wrong.
Do set quoted source text in 楷書.
donts: Don't give a page its own background colour or dark skin; pigments live only in seals.
Don't use green for good or red for bad.
Don't add glows, gradient text, coloured side stripes or kicker labels above headings.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons; draw SVG at the tab-bar stroke weight.
